newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee called $100 up, may stop at $50.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee called $100 up, may stop at $50.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
LIFFE coffee futures were due to open $100 up on Tuesday on numbers based on the rally in New York on Monday. But traders said in practice, it could stop at $50.
Technically, analysts said a break above the most recent high of $1,645, basis September, would indicate a swift move to the $1,700 level and near the lows seen in June.
Trevor Neil, senior technical analyst at Union Cal Futures, said coffee would meet small resistance at the most recent high of $1,645.
"A break of that would indicate a swift move to $1,700 and near the lows in July," he said. "Above that there is substantial resistance that could stall the market."
Neil said technically the market still bearish in the intermediate term. "I expect the rally to peter out quickly," he said.
Initial support is seen at $1,585 but the must-hold support level is last week's floor of $1,477 -- the lowest level in six months.

Arabica futures on the New York market ran up to near six-week highs Monday, on speculative and trade buying amid concerns of a shortage of exchange-certified coffee for delivery against the September contract.
Benchmark September surged 12.05 cents per lb -- or nearly seven percent -- on the day, to 188.35 cents, its highest settlement since June 17.
The rise accelerated after September breached key resistance at 184.50 cents, a double top on the charts, and triggered buy-stops near 185.00 cents. --Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
